ops.title: Release tags must be annotated (git tag -a), never lightweight
ops.body:
`git tag vX.Y.Z origin/main` creates a **lightweight** tag (a plain ref to the commit). The Release workflow's first job, `verify-tag-on-main` (the shared `yasyf/homebrew-tap/.github/actions/verify-tag-on-main` action), rejects it:

```
remote ref is not an annotated tag object (type='commit'); lightweight tags are forbidden
```

Every downstream job — helper app, pure CLI matrix, smoke, publish release, bump-formula — depends on that gate, so all of them skip. Nothing builds, no release is created, no assets upload.

**The version number is then burned.** A repository ruleset blocks tag deletion on origin:

```
! [remote rejected] v0.47.7 (push declined due to repository rule violations)
```

So the bad tag cannot be removed or replaced, and the release must move to the next patch version. This is how v0.47.7 was lost (2026-07-25): tagged lightweight, gate failed, tag undeletable, release re-cut as v0.47.8 on the same commit ba1eaa9.

**Always cut release tags as:**

```
git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "vX.Y.Z

<one-line summary>" <commit-on-main>
git cat-file -t vX.Y.Z    # must print "tag", not "commit"
git push origin vX.Y.Z
```

Verify the `cat-file -t` output *before* pushing — that check is the entire difference between a release and a permanently wasted version number. Note this is separate from the AGENTS.md rule about never re-tagging a *published* stable version; here nothing published, but the ruleset still makes the tag immutable.
ops.when: Before cutting a cc-notes release tag, or when a Release workflow run fails at verify-tag-on-main
